A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimMark by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original SimMark detection, text-quality, sentence-drop and ablation results, alongside comparisons drawn from prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains original SimMark experiments and adds Gemma3-4B evaluations, merging attacks, sampling-budget and latency experiments, and a human study.

M1.justification: The rejection-sampling procedure, consecutive-sentence similarity measures, optional PCA, soft counting and detection statistic remain unchanged. The revised black-box description and additional model configurations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: RealNews, BookSum and Reddit-TIFU remain the datasets. v2 adds a sentence-merging attack scenario and a small human watermark-identification task, while removing the BookSum sentence-drop scenario shown in v1 Figure 3.

E2.justification: v2 adds UW across all three datasets in Table 1 and to the sentence-perturbation comparisons, adds SIR for Reddit-TIFU, and adds UW, KGW and SIR to text-quality Table 2. These additions substantially broaden comparisons, particularly against token-level methods.

E3.justification: New Gemma3-4B experiments use 300-token generations, different similarity intervals and a BookSum-calibrated threshold transferred across datasets. Budget-sweep, latency and human-study protocols are added. v2 specifies 10 GPT-3.5 bigram candidates versus v1's unqualified 25-candidate description; this revises the reported setting without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds merging-attack robustness, threshold-transfer testing, sampling-budget sensitivity, measured runtime and human imperceptibility analyses (Figure 4; Appendices D–F and M). The original soft-count and PCA ablations are retained unchanged as Tables 6–7. The BookSum sentence-drop analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Section 4 of v2 newly states that results are from a single run; v1 supplies no run count. This is a disclosure change, with no added confidence intervals, repeated-run variability or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 16 shared Table 1 rows remain numerically unchanged, but v2 adds baseline, Gemma, merging, budget, latency and human-study results. Table 2 revises semantic entropy, including unwatermarked text from 3.10 to 3.32 and SemStamp from 3.17 to 3.32. The separate Euclidean text-quality row and BookSum sentence-drop results are removed.

T1.justification: The soft-count and z-score equations, histogram estimate of p0, and geometric sampling calculation remain unchanged. v2 Appendix G's theoretical analysis retains v1's derivation of approximately 5.1 samples from probability 0.194.

C1.justification: The central claims about black-box compatibility, paraphrase robustness, quality preservation and sampling efficiency remain. v2 narrows the conclusion's superiority claim to sentence-level methods and removes v1's assertion that resistance to reverse engineering ensures resilience against spoofing.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for weaker detection on short texts, token-level advantages under merging, and the runtime–robustness tradeoff. Its limitations explicitly recognize spoofing through approximate reconstruction using public embeddings or PCA data, substantially qualifying v1's security interpretation. Existing overhead, mixed-text and interval limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds dataset split identifiers, model variants and sizes, MarkLLM configurations, the Transformers timing implementation, and participant instructions. It also documents settings for the new experiments. Existing hardware specifications, core hyperparameters, paraphrasing prompts and code-access link are largely retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 substantially expands positioning against post-hoc watermarking through PostMark, Yang et al. and Hao et al., discussing access requirements, cost, quality and robustness. Additional contextual and implementation references are introduced. SemStamp's publication update is the same cited work, not a new comparator.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: future work becomes a main limitations section, portions of related work and experimental settings move into appendices, and supplementary sections are rearranged. The introduction, method exposition and discussion are extensively edited, including replacing the posthoc characterization with black-box generation language.

P2.justification: The document adopts an EMNLP layout and adds radar summaries, a sampling-budget figure, Gemma, latency and human-study tables, and a participant-instruction image. The attack figure replaces its BookSum panel with RealNews merging results and adds UW. Existing examples and ablation displays are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's single-model validation and sampling-count-based efficiency evidence through Gemma tests, stronger baseline and attack comparisons, and measured runtime costs. It also replaces an unsupported spoofing-resilience assurance with explicit limitations. Single-run evidence and the three-person human study remain limited, and BookSum drop-attack and separate Euclidean quality results are removed. Nevertheless, the broader validation and clearer practical boundaries substantially improve the paper's evidential support.
